why: The ministry's own launch of Temekoun, the national platform giving civil servants basic digital skills across their careers, is the instrument itself rather than commentary on it, and it names the competences covered.
The only quantified addition to civil-service digital skills inside the window: a twelve-week cybersecurity and AI programme launched for 300 civil servants by two ministers jointly.
A second distinct event that moves capability building from one-off courses to a standing national continuing-training framework, with the digital ministry co-chairing.
The standing authoritative assessment of population digital skills, with a dedicated chapter and a ministerial preface; it settles that no measured national digital-literacy rate exists.

The only quantified general-population digital-skills series inside the window: D-CLIC trained 101 in 2023 and 272 across 2024-2025, with 300 currently in training and a further 300-place programme announced.
The Ecole Numerique programme is the standing instrument for digital-transformation training in Mauritanian schooling, and the ministry page gives its concrete starting position.
A completed step rather than a plan: a digital system actually used across 195 centres for 64,532 candidates at the 2026 baccalaureat to assign invigilators and centre heads at random.
A distinct earlier event: the two ministers agreeing the roadmap for digitising exam organisation and marking, with phased testing and rollout from the following school year.
The founding document of Ain, the national citizen-complaint portal, setting out its scope, the round-the-clock sectoral representatives, the ten-day response rule and the explicit exclusions.
The most recent authoritative publication of the series: the first twelve months reported to the Council of Ministers, 17,965 items, 97 percent processed, handling time down to seven days.

The national e-participation policy is the instrument itself, setting the vision, the e-information, e-consultation and e-decision axes, the governance bodies and the starting UN e-participation score.
The movement most directly on the indicator, and a primary procurement document: the citizen-participation platform passing from policy to a provisional contract award.
A second distinct event and a completed step: the report of the first preparatory phase of the national dialogue delivered to the President, with the scale of the consultation stated.

The Mauritanian instrument that both states the sex-disaggregated position in digital financial services and sets the corrective policy, naming women as a target group with their share of account holders and mobile-money customers.
A completed step rather than an announcement: two ministries jointly marking Girls in ICT Day 2026 and awarding the prizes of a national challenge for women-led AI and digital-innovation start-ups.
A distinct event: the release of the Mauritania component of Global Findex 2025, the only nationally representative demand-side series from which the country's digital gender gaps can be computed.

The founding Mauritanian legal text in full, including the accessibility articles bearing on digital and information services and the creation of the disability card on which access to services turns.

The most quantified movement in the window: a package worth about 1.899 billion old ouguiyas including cash transfers for 6,000 disabled children, plus the standing position of over 18,000 disability cards issued.

A second distinct event and the most structurally significant: the national human-rights institution telling the Universal Periodic Review that the application decrees of law 043-2006 have been promulgated.

The operative national asylum instrument, superseding the 2005 decree; article 15 gives refugees national treatment for health care, the labour market, social security and education, which is the rule the indicator turns on.

The quantified position for the window and the one document tying registration to services: biometric identity management, the National Identification Number issued with ANRPTS, birth certificates, SIGE-R in schools and 8,263 households paid under Tekavoul.

A distinct event on the service-integration side with completed steps stated by the Ministry of Health: four camp health units handed to government services and service quality rising from 31 to 90 percent.

The operational action plan of the national broadband and universal-access strategy, so the instrument for closing the divide; the regulator's annual report and volume 1 of the same study were already staged by concurrent slices.

The structural movement on the financing instrument itself: the Council of Ministers replacing the 2020 decree governing the universal-access fund and bringing it inside the State budgetary framework.
A distinct completed event: the first digital service desk in the interior wilayas, at Bassikounou, with 20 local young people trained to assist users and free connected devices provided.
